scenes.shot: about.html at the top: title, lead, authors; cursor still
scenes.text: STRATA is a point-in-time checker for machine learning pipelines over time-stamped relational data, made for code that coding agents write. It runs the code on the data as it is and on the data as it was at prediction time, and reports where the two disagree.

scenes.shot: scroll to the slider; drag t from 2017-10 to 2018-01-01; the review turns red, the table shows 4 against 3
scenes.text: One product from the Olist marketplace, its orders and their reviews. A feature that counts reviews of past orders also counts this review, written after t. In the data as of t, it does not exist yet: four against three. That difference is the witness STRATA reports.

scenes.shot: scroll to the five-layer table, then to the rule in large type
scenes.text: The future can get in at five places: the task table, the features, the training rows of the model, the examples given to a language model, and the agent's own memory of the entities. One rule covers all five: the output on the full database must equal the output on the database as of t.

scenes.shot: scroll past the schema commands to the Results table; pause on the first row; scroll back up and click Open the demo
scenes.text: All STRATA needs is one short schema per database, drafted from the raw files and reviewed once. On eight benchmark databases it caught all forty-three leaking code changes and flagged none of the fifty-five harmless ones. Now the demo.

scenes.shot: index.html opens with feature_program.py; cursor slowly across the editor, the diagnosis pane and the console
scenes.text: The workbench. On the left, a feature program that a code model wrote for Olist. On the right, the diagnosis and a console. Every console output is a recorded strata run on the real data.

scenes.shot: click Run check; wait for LEAK; cursor over the witness row, then over the highlighted lines in the editor
scenes.text: Run check. The verdict is leak. The witness names the time, the product, the column, both values, and the table the difference came from: reviews. The program cuts orders at t, but joins every review, including the ones written later.

scenes.shot: click Apply fix; the editor jumps to the green lines; click Run check; wait for CLEAN
scenes.text: The suggested fix cuts reviews at their creation date. Apply it, run again. Clean at every tested time, for the witness run, for the canary with a rewritten future, and for the unknown-column probe.

scenes.shot: example 'Features that drop cancelled orders'; Run check; wait for UNCHECKABLE; cursor on the column list
scenes.text: A second program drops cancelled orders. Olist keeps only the latest status, so the status at t cannot be rebuilt from the data. STRATA answers uncheckable and lists the output columns that depend on it.

scenes.shot: click Schema; click With the LLM agent; click the orders table; cursor on the reason; close
scenes.text: The schema behind these verdicts is drafted from the raw files. With the language model agent, every decision comes with a reason, and the order status is marked as a snapshot, valid only at the end of the data.

scenes.shot: database RelBench F1, example 'Agent-written training script'; Run check; cursor on the top bars of the chart, then on the AUC row
scenes.text: The model layer. A training script written by a coding agent for RelBench Formula One, run exactly as it is, with and without the four hundred and twelve race results that came after t. Predictions move by up to zero point eight seven, and the AUC jumps from zero point seven one to zero point nine three. The metric alone would have missed this.

scenes.shot: database RelBench Event; Run check; cursor on the red cells
scenes.text: The agent layer replaces every ID with a made-up one, twice. This script turns the IDs into numbers, so the two renamings disagree, and the answer is uncheckable.

scenes.shot: end.html: the end card; hold for the whole sentence
scenes.text: Five layers, one rule, and exit codes a coding agent can act on. Install STRATA, draft the schema, drop the skill file into your agent, and it runs the check before it reports a score.
